description.narrative: Initiative Name: Agro-ecological transition for improved livelihoods and welfare of smallholders in remote and upland areas: A pilot initiative for ethnic minority smallholders participating in the cassia value chain in Lao Cai province. Objective: Create sustainable livelihoods for EM women in cinnamon-growing households in Bao Nhai and Coc Lau communes, by piloting a transition to agroecological cinnamon production with gender equality integration. Duration: December 2025 – May 2027 (18 months) Project areas: Bảo Nhai and Cốc Lầu communes, Lào Cai province Direct beneficiaries: 100 EM farmers (at least 75% women) representing 100 cinnamon-growing households in Bao Nhai and Coc Lau communes will have their agroecological cinnamon production techniques improved, increasing productivity and product quality, thereby diversifying livelihoods and improving income. Activities: Result 1: Establish and enhance the capacity of women-led cinnamon production groups 1. Conduct a baseline survey; (2). Capacity building for project staff and partners; (3). Develop technical training materials (4). Support establishment and operation of 4 women-led groups; (5). Provide technicalsupport and promote farmer sharing via monthly meetings;(6). Organize training courses on cinnamon agroforestry techniques with gender integration, group management skills, harvesting and processing, market standards and variety selection...(7). Support digital tools for yield recording and monitoring; (8). Establish a community nursery and( 9).Training on nursery techniques. Result 2: Expandthe cinnamon area meeting sustainable/ecological standards/certifications. (1). Organize events with experts, enterprises, and certification bodies on standards/certifications; (2). Conduct technical and credit/capital access consultancy sessions; (3). Conduct quality monitoring sessions with stakeholder participation and (4). Support for evaluation, documentation preparation, and part of thefees for the first registration. Result 3: Sustainable and inclusive cinnamon value chains are established through multi-stakeholder platforms/forums (1) Organize consultation meetings with enterprises to establish the ecological value chain; (2). Organize thematic meetings and join annual cinnamon sector events hosted by VPSA and PPP; (3). Organize market linkage events to update farmer groups on market demand and standards and (4). Support group members in joining trade fairs. Result 4: Model integration into local development plans (1). Conduct a comprehensive study on the local cinnamon sector to assess market potential, policies on planning, management, and sustainable development; (2). Organize stakeholder meetings to guide integration of agroecology and gender mainstreaminginto planning and policy. (3). Organize a provincial workshop to share lessons learned and promote a cinnamon sector plan integrating agroecological solutions and GM, adapted to local conditions and market needs.
